doc.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

chapter: Childhood in China and move to Japan
title: Father's business and the Japanese community in Manchuria
summary: Her father's textile-company and import/export career, and growing up in a separate Japanese community and school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Export/import. He was sent to China, in those days called Manchuria, by a big company, a textile company, a Japanese textile company, and they made a big plant in a place called Yoyo [sic]. So that’s why my parents left. And after that he left and started his own business. But one thing about when you’re very young you can endure a lot I think.
It must have been quite a culture shock.
Well China and Japan — my history is not great — but they’ve had a checkered history over the years. Was it difficult to go from one to the other?

No. Because we all did it — what they call they have a Japanese school. The Japanese community is quite different from the Chinese community. We were in a Japanese community. You know a funny thing about it — 30 years ago I was back in China, now they call it the Yunnan Province old Manchuria, and I visited my own, where I was born, where I went to school, and I didn’t realize until then this was down by Inische [sic], and we had a separate community. You know I was too little to realize that. My father’s right arm man was a Chinese, and we visited their home and he used to visit our home frequently. And I never realized that we were indeed a separate community I think. So the school we went to, and I never thought about it but there wasn’t any Chinese, maybe one or two pupils, but all were Japanese. So all the Japanese education and everything, the old teacher came from the mainland Japan. So there was nothing about that. But we had a Chinese language mandatory class started third year I think it was, the third year. That was mandatory. So we had to learn Chinese, a very difficult language.
